headline: Denver Conference Previews the 2028 Field as Shapiro Steps Forward and Van Hollen Steps Aside
summary: Ten days after the midterms, would-be 2028 candidates tested their messages at the What's Next conference in Denver on November 13. Gov. Josh Shapiro, whom CNN describes as expected to run, gave a campaign-style speech and said he would be doing his part. Sen. Elissa Slotkin said she is seriously considering a run, Sen. Cory Booker said he is giving it hard thought, and Rep. Ro Khanna said the reception made him more likely to consider it. Nobody has formally declared.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who had previously expressed interest in a presidential run, told reporters he is not running in 2028 and is instead challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader in a December 1 vote. Pete Buttigieg said he would have no news on 2028 anytime soon, and Sen. Ruben Gallego said his three young children weigh heavily on his decision.

Odds moves are small this week. Shapiro rises a point on his post-election momentum, and Gallego slips a point. We add Booker and Slotkin to the board, moving their chances out of the unlisted field, which falls from 18 to 15 percent. Ossoff won a straw poll of 990 activists at Crooked Media's conference on November 7 and still leads prediction markets near 27 percent, but he says he is not running, so we hold him at 8. A CNN/SSRS poll taken before the midterms found Democrats about equally excited by Harris, Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg.

candidates.name: Gavin Newsom
candidates.title: Governor of California (term ends January 2027)
candidates.bio: Newsom was mayor of San Francisco and lieutenant governor before becoming governor in 2019. He is term-limited and leaves office in January 2027. He has built a national profile through confrontations with President Trump and a redistricting push in California.
candidates.outlook: Newsom has a firm decision date, early January, and a clear public condition: he says he would not run against Harris. That conditional keeps his odds tied to hers. Prediction markets are cooler on him than they were earlier this year, while national polls keep him in second place.

headlines.text: Newsom told Turkey's Anadolu news agency he will decide on a 2028 run in early January, after time with his family.
Newsom told CNN he would not run if Harris does, calling a contest between the two California Democrats mutually destructive.
headlines.source: The National News Desk via FOX 11

quotes.text: So we'll spend the next few weeks with the family and make a decision early January.

candidates.name: Kamala Harris
candidates.title: Former Vice President of the United States
candidates.bio: Harris was California attorney general, a U.S. senator, and vice president from 2021 to 2025. She was the Democratic nominee in 2024. She declined to run for governor of California in 2026 and campaigned for Democrats in the midterms.
candidates.outlook: Harris leads most national polling averages, in the mid-20s, and 27 percent of Democrats in a pre-midterm CNN/SSRS poll said they would be excited to support her, tied for the most. Prediction markets put her near 5 percent, and she finished far back in the Crooked Con activist straw poll. She has not decided, and Newsom's pledge not to run against her means her choice shapes the whole field.

headlines.text: Harris told the Associated Press the day after the midterms that she wants to help steer the party whether or not she runs again.
A CNN/SSRS poll found Harris, Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg drew the most excitement among Democrats, though Harris also had the largest share who said they would never back her.
MS NOW reported that Harris has not settled on another run and is focused on helping Democrats win Congress.

quotes.text: Whether I’m in office or not, that’s the role I feel compelled to play.
I have not decided if I'm going to run again.

candidates.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
candidates.title: U.S. Representative from New York
candidates.bio: Ocasio-Cortez has represented parts of the Bronx and Queens since 2019. She toured the country with Sen. Bernie Sanders in 2025 and has become one of the best-known progressives in the party.
candidates.outlook: She has said she would decide after the midterms between a presidential run and a Senate challenge to Chuck Schumer, and she has not yet announced a choice. Prediction markets rate her second, near 15 percent, and the New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America voted on November 14 to urge her to run. A Senate run would be a lower-risk path, which holds her odds below the top tier.

headlines.text: The New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America voted 291 to 123 to encourage her to run for president, though a sizable minority dissented.
In a pre-midterm CNN/SSRS poll, 27 percent of Democrats said they would be excited to support her, tied with Harris for the most.
The Intercept reported that progressives see no obvious alternative to her for a left-wing run, while some strategists say a Senate bid would be easier.

quotes.text: I haven't ruled out the possibility, and I'm very humbled [by] the tremendous amount of support out there.

candidates.name: Pete Buttigieg
candidates.title: Former U.S. Secretary of Transportation
candidates.bio: Buttigieg was mayor of South Bend, Indiana, and finished among the top candidates in the 2020 Democratic primary. He served as Transportation Secretary from 2021 to 2025.
candidates.outlook: Buttigieg has said he leans toward running, but he told reporters in Denver he would have no news on 2028 anytime soon. He placed third in the Crooked Con straw poll and drew excitement from 26 percent of Democrats in the CNN/SSRS poll. Prediction markets price him near 5 percent, reflecting doubts about his support among Black voters ahead of a calendar that opens in South Carolina.

headlines.text: Buttigieg told reporters at a Democratic conference in Denver that he would not have news on a 2028 run anytime soon, though he has not ruled one out.
Buttigieg said on a podcast in August that he is leaning toward running in 2028 but that much is still unknown.
headlines.source: The National News Desk via FOX 11

quotes.text: I think I'm more inclined than not, but there's so much we don't know.
quotes.source: The National News Desk via FOX 11

candidates.name: Josh Shapiro
candidates.title: Governor of Pennsylvania
candidates.bio: Shapiro was Pennsylvania attorney general before winning the governorship in 2022. He was on Kamala Harris's vice presidential shortlist in 2024 and was re-elected on November 3, 2026.
candidates.outlook: Up one point. Shapiro followed his decisive re-election with a campaign-style speech in Denver, and CNN reports that he is expected to launch a bid. He says the timing is a family decision and will not commit yet. National polls have him in the mid single digits and many Democrats still do not know him, but his swing-state record makes him the strongest governor in the field on paper.

headlines.text: Shapiro gave a campaign-style speech at the What's Next summit in Denver, urging national Democrats to follow Pennsylvania's lead on wages, housing and abortion rights.
Asked about a 2028 timeline, Shapiro said it was a decision for his family and that he would speak when ready.
Shapiro won re-election by a wide margin and used his victory to argue that Democrats must govern responsibly with their new congressional power.

quotes.text: I've decided to be a loud voice in this process that we're going through right now as a party to put ourselves in the best position to compete.
It needs to be a sobering moment for Democrats. We got the keys to the car and now we have to drive it responsibly.

candidates.name: JB Pritzker
candidates.title: Governor of Illinois
candidates.bio: Pritzker, a billionaire and heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune, has been governor of Illinois since 2019. He has been a leading Democratic critic of President Trump and has funded abortion-rights and other Democratic causes.
candidates.outlook: Pritzker won a third term on November 3, the first Illinois governor to do so since 1982, and told supporters they were at the base of another mountain. He has not ruled out a run. Wealth gives him a financial advantage, though his profile outside Illinois is thinner than that of the top contenders.

headlines.text: Pritzker won a third term as Illinois governor and spoke in his victory remarks about the next challenge without addressing 2028 directly.

quotes.text: We climbed one mountain tonight. But we are sitting at the base of another.

candidates.name: Andy Beshear
candidates.title: Governor of Kentucky
candidates.bio: Beshear was Kentucky attorney general before winning the governorship in 2019 and was re-elected in 2023, both times in a state that voted heavily for Donald Trump. He chairs the Democratic Governors Association.
candidates.outlook: Beshear has said he is considering a run, has pitched Democratic governors as the party's face, and has held early talks with potential campaign staff, according to the Associated Press. Prediction markets price him around 4 percent. His red-state record is his main argument. He has not set a date for a decision.

headlines.text: The Associated Press reported that Beshear has held preliminary conversations with potential presidential campaign staff.
The Denver Gazette reported that Beshear and other Democratic governors are positioning themselves as a pragmatic alternative for 2028.

quotes.text: I think Democratic governors should be the face of the Democratic Party

candidates.name: Mark Kelly
candidates.title: U.S. Senator from Arizona
candidates.bio: Kelly is a retired Navy captain and former astronaut who has represented Arizona in the Senate since 2020. He drew national attention after the Pentagon moved to demote him over a video urging service members to refuse illegal orders, and he sued Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over it.
candidates.outlook: Kelly said he would not decide until after the midterms, and the Associated Press reports he has already talked with potential campaign staff. He polls in the mid single digits, and 22 percent of Democrats in the CNN/SSRS poll said they would be excited to back him. His military record and his clash with the administration are assets, but he lacks a large national base.

headlines.text: The Associated Press reported that Kelly has held preliminary conversations with potential presidential campaign staff.
Kelly said at the Atlantic Festival that he would not decide on a presidential run until after the election and that his family gets a say.

quotes.text: I'm not gonna decide until after this election, because I do really believe we need to be focused on this.

candidates.name: Ro Khanna
candidates.title: U.S. Representative from California
candidates.bio: Khanna has represented a Silicon Valley district since 2017 and was a national co-chair of Bernie Sanders's 2020 campaign. He has built a profile on economic nationalism, Medicare for All and opposition to foreign wars.
candidates.outlook: Khanna told reporters in Denver he is certainly considering a run and that the reception there made him more likely to, and he expects candidates to start entering next year. Allies launched a draft group, Run Ro, on November 5, and he says he will decide with his family after the holidays. Progressives are not unified behind him, and he competes for the same lane as Ocasio-Cortez.

headlines.text: Khanna said at the Denver conference, organized by a centrist group, that he is certainly considering a 2028 run and is testing whether his message resonates.
Allies of Khanna, including former Rep. Jamaal Bowman, launched a draft campaign two days after the midterms.

quotes.text: I think after the reception here, I'm more likely to consider it. I mean, but I'm going around the country seeing whether the message will resonate.
Whether I run or support someone else is something I will decide with my family after the holidays.

candidates.name: Ruben Gallego
candidates.title: U.S. Senator from Arizona
candidates.bio: Gallego is a Marine Corps veteran who served in the U.S. House from 2015 to 2025 and was elected to the Senate in 2024. He has emphasized working-class voters, including Latino men.
candidates.outlook: Down one point. Gallego said in Denver that his three young children will weigh heavily on his decision and that he would have to work out how to run without personal wealth. His October economic plan was read as groundwork for a campaign, but he starts from a low base nationally, under 1 percent in prediction markets, and shares a home state with Kelly.

headlines.text: Gallego told reporters that raising three young children would be a major factor in whether he runs.
Gallego released an economic plan that includes a tax on data centers and a robot tax meant to protect workers from automation.

quotes.text: I have three kids — 9, 3 and a 1-year-old. You know, it's hard to manage that schedule, and I have to figure out how to still be a good dad and run for office
So, we don't want to have a tax system that is designed to actually encourage automation.

candidates.name: Jon Ossoff
candidates.title: U.S. Senator from Georgia
candidates.bio: Jon Ossoff has represented Georgia in the U.S. Senate since 2021 and won a second term on November 3, 2026. A former investigative journalist, he is the youngest sitting Democratic senator.
candidates.outlook: Prediction markets rank him first, near 27 percent, and he won the Crooked Con activist straw poll with 38 percent. But he has said repeatedly that he is not running and pledged at an October debate to serve his full six-year term. We take the pledge seriously and hold him well below his market price, but a swing-state winner this popular with the party stays on the board until the field is set.

headlines.text: Ossoff was the first choice of 38.4 percent of 990 attendees in a straw poll at Crooked Con, Crooked Media's progressive conference, ahead of Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg.
Asked at a Georgia Senate debate whether he would serve a full term, Ossoff said yes and repeated that he is not running for president.

quotes.text: I have zero interest in running for president. I'm not running for president. I'm running for re-election to the Senate.

candidates.name: Cory Booker
candidates.title: U.S. Senator from New Jersey
candidates.bio: Booker was mayor of Newark before winning a Senate seat in 2013, and he ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2020. He won re-election to a third full term on November 3, 2026.
candidates.outlook: New to the board this week. Booker told Fox News he is giving a 2028 run a lot of hard thought, and the Associated Press reports he starts the cycle with more than $20 million in his federal campaign account. His 2020 campaign ended before the first votes, and prediction markets give him under 1 percent.

headlines.text: Booker said in Denver that he is giving a 2028 campaign serious thought while focusing on what he calls an American renewal.
The Associated Press reported that Booker begins the 2028 cycle with more than $20 million in his federal campaign account after an election-night speech that left little doubt about his ambitions.

quotes.text: The gap I’m concerned about is not the gap between left and right anymore. It’s a gap between the American people and the American dream, and I want to see that gap close

candidates.name: Elissa Slotkin
candidates.title: U.S. Senator from Michigan
candidates.bio: Slotkin is a former CIA analyst and Pentagon official who represented a Michigan House district from 2019 to 2025. She was elected to the Senate in 2024.
candidates.outlook: New to the board this week. Slotkin told reporters in Denver she is seriously considering a run, and she has said she will not vote for Schumer as leader. She tied for 16th in the Crooked Con straw poll and is under 1 percent in prediction markets, so she starts near the bottom.

headlines.text: Slotkin told reporters at the Denver conference that she is seriously considering a 2028 presidential run but has not decided.

quotes.text: I haven't made any decisions. Whether it's me or somebody else, I just want to be a part of that next generation of leaders going forward that does things differently and understands who they serve

results.summary: Jon Ossoff was the first choice of 38.4 percent of 990 attendees at Crooked Media's progressive conference, followed by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 16.6 percent and Pete Buttigieg at about 14 percent. It is an unscientific poll of activists.

Democrats won control of the House and Senate and a majority of governorships. As of November 10 they had flipped at least seven Senate seats, including Texas, Ohio and North Carolina, with Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled along with 19 House races.
JB Pritzker defeated Republican Darren Bailey to win a third term.

The full Democratic National Committee approved by voice vote a calendar that puts South Carolina first, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia. States that go out of order lose all of their delegates and face a $270,000 fine.

calendar.note: Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer in a closed-ballot vote.
Newsom says he will decide after spending the next few weeks with his family.
calendar.label: Early Jan 2027

calendar.note: First contest on the DNC calendar.
State law requires New Hampshire to go first, which conflicts with the DNC calendar.

out.name: Chris Van Hollen
out.note: said on November 13, 2026, that he is not running in 2028, as he challenges Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
